correctness.rationale: Every commuting pair has the idempotent common product h=ef=fe with im(h)=Fix(e)∩Fix(f); each interval fiber of h is e,f-invariant. On any rooted fiber the compositions equal its root iff, on each side, at most one retraction has a nonroot fixed point; necessity is a monotonicity contradiction and sufficiency follows because a retraction with no fixed point on that side is constant to the root. An anchored side of length a has H_a retractions with generating function H(t)=(1-t)/(1-3t+t^2), via gaps of length d with d monotone cuts. The two maps can contribute nontrivial fixed points on exactly one side-owner, giving 2H_a−1 local choices. Fibers of h concatenate freely and uniquely, yielding the claimed uB/(1-uB), B=t(2H−1/(1-t))^2. Aperiodic positive coefficients and monotonicity give unique dominant simple pole r, and differentiation in rank variable yields Kn+O(1). Exact B(1/6)=5766/9025<1 proves exponential base <1. Exhaustive direct composition confirms all rank profiles for n=1..9 (7,817,630 candidate pairs); finite checks are not the proof. All hypotheses n≥1, total monotone transformations, and ordered pairs are explicit.

value.rationale: Compatible commuting retractions and the rank of their common product are intrinsic structural invariants of a natural, well-studied chain-transformation monoid. The exact product-rank enumerator retains genuine information lost by individual-idempotent Fibonacci counts, identifies a new local obstruction (no opposite-source nonroot fixed points on either side of a common-product root), and yields a nontrivial simple-pole growth law, sharp exponential rarity of commutativity, and a linear expected product rank. The result is uniform over every chain length and not an arbitrary numerical slice, renaming, or routine finite check.
